bullets.title: How to “Dry Age” a Steak in Two Hours
bullets.note:
“Dry-aged steak is famously tender and flavorful, but often too expensive for home cooks to attempt. In this episode of _Techniquely_, [Lan Lam](https://www.instagram.com/lan_cooks) explains how dry-aging works and shows us how to achieve the flavor of dry-aging at home in as little as 2 hours with the use of shio koji, a fermented Japanese paste.” Chef David Chang of Momofuku fame also [swears by koji](https://www.tastingtable.com/1325953/david-chang-use-koji-cooking/).**​  
​  
​**Shio koji (塩麹) is a traditional Japanese seasoning made by fermenting a mixture of koji (rice inoculated with _Aspergillus oryzae_), salt, and water. It’s prized for its ability to tenderize meat, enhance umami, and balance saltiness with subtle sweetness—often referred to as a “natural MSG.”
